nodes.summary: A natural number $N$ is a Keith number with digit list $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{k-1})$ when $k \ge 2$, $d_i < 10$ for every $i$, $d_0 \ne 0$, $N = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} d_i \cdot 10^{k-1-i}$ (so $d$ is the decimal representation of $N$, with at least two digits), and $N = a_m$ for some $m \ge k$, where $(a_m)_{m \ge 0}$ is the Keith sequence of $d$ indexed from $0$ (so $N$ occurs after the initial digits).
nodes.title: Keith number with given digits

nodes.summary: A natural number $N$ is a Keith number when it is a Keith number with some digit list: that is, $N$ has a decimal representation $d_0 d_1 \cdots d_{k-1}$ with $k \ge 2$ digits and leading digit $d_0 \ne 0$, and $N = a_j$ for some $j \ge k$, where $(a_m)_{m \ge 0}$ is the Keith sequence of $(d_0, \dots, d_{k-1})$: $a_m = d_m$ for $m < k$, and each later term is the sum of the preceding $k$ terms.
nodes.title: Keith number

nodes.summary: Given a list $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{k-1})$ of natural numbers and $j \in \mathbb{N}$, the Keith sequence prefix of $d$ at step $j$ is the list of length $k + j$ obtained from $d$ by appending, $j$ times, the sum of the last $k$ entries of the current list. This is the recurrence used for Keith numbers.
nodes.title: Keith sequence prefix

nodes.summary: Given a list $d = (d_0, \dots, d_{k-1})$ of natural numbers, the Keith sequence of $d$ is the sequence $(a_m)_{m \ge 0}$ with $a_m = d_m$ for $m < k$ and $a_m = \sum_{i=m-k}^{m-1} a_i$ for $m \ge k$: after the initial entries, each term is the sum of the preceding $k$ terms.
nodes.title: Keith sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
